title: Annotate in a narrow margin rail
intent: Give definitions, sources, and asides a home without breaking the reading line.
when_to_use: the text needs repeated small annotations: figures, sources, definitions, alternative phrasings
the reader benefits from a reference layer at the same position on every screen
when_not_to_use: the annotations are load bearing and must be read in sequence, where they belong in the body
the annotation count per screen is below two, where inline parentheses are cheaper
rules: the rail holds at most three entries per screen, each under 20 words
each entry aligns to the line it annotates, or to the top of its paragraph when the line is unknown
the rail is a labelled repeated structure with a visible column heading, never a loose paragraph set beside a headline
below the layout switch the rail collapses into inline notes and the note text does not change
trade_off: The rail costs a third of the width on a desktop and forces annotations to be short, which pushes long explanations into the body and makes the document longer.
failure_mode: The rail becomes a second article, and the reader alternates between two columns of equal weight with no signal about which one continues the argument.

example.brief: Technical explainer where each figure needs a source and a caveat.
example.ruling: Family side-annotation-margin: 68 character body column, one narrow right rail headed Notes, at most three notes per screen, each tied to a paragraph and collapsed inline on narrow viewports.
